ledger.claim: The driver never satisfied the contact obligation POL-NS-23 imposes before a no-show cancellation. The chat log for this trip carries two messages, both sent by the RIDER (21:16:40 and 21:19:30), and message_count of driver messages is zero; the only call in the record is the rider's own call at 21:20:10, which rang 30 s and was not answered. There was therefore neither an in-app message nor an in-app call placed by the driver before the 21:23:15 cancellation. Under POL-NS-23 both limbs are required and either one missing voids the fee: the 5.00 SGD charged must be refunded in full with no driver compensation.

The driver failed to reach the pickup by the deadline POL-NS-24 sets. Pickup was scheduled for 21:15:00, so the 300 s allowance carried on this policy (driver_late_after_scheduled_sec) fixes the deadline at 21:20:00. The trip record's arrived_by_deadline is false and arrived_at is null; the rider cancelled at 21:23:15, after the deadline had passed. On POL-NS-24 the rider was entitled to cancel at no charge and any fee charged is refunded in full (FULL_REFUND).

The code-derived arrival check in the GPS artifact records nearest_fix as null and corroborated as false, tested against the 50 m arrival radius POL-NS-21 sets for a STANDARD pickup zone, and the trip record's arrived_at is null. The trace itself shows the vehicle reporting a constant 0 kph from 21:09:30 through the 21:23:00 fix, i.e. stationary for the last stretch of the booking until the moment of cancellation. The driver never came within the arrival radius, so the arrival event POL-NS-21 requires before anything can be earned is absent.

The driver's written answer, 'I was coming', is not borne out by the machine record. The only GPS artifact for the trip (complete: 49 fixes, 100% coverage, no gap over 120 s, every fix reporting accuracy) shows the driver's speeds falling to 0 kph at 21:09:30 and remaining at 0 for every fix to 21:23:00, while the code-derived arrival check records no corroborated arrival. A statement that he was on his way cannot outweigh a trace showing a stationary vehicle up to the cancellation.

The free wait under POL-NS-21 never ran on this booking. This was a scheduled trip and the free wait starts from the driver's arrival where he did not arrive before the scheduled time; arrived_at is null, so the timer had no start, and it can never be said to have expired. POL-NS-21 permits cancellation as a no-show only after the free wait; with the wait unstarted, no no-show charge could be earned at any point before the rider cancelled.

POL-NS-22 charges the 5.00 SGD no-show fee when the driver cancels after the free wait. The precondition is missing here: the trip record shows cancelled_by RIDER, status CANCELLED_BY_RIDER and cancellation_reason_code RIDER_CANCELLED, the driver never arrived, and the free wait never began. The 5.00 SGD cancellation-fee line on the payments ledger therefore rests on no condition the policy recognises, and nothing is owed to the driver as compensation for time and fuel on a trip he never reached.

The record carries no traffic evidence at all: EV-ADVIS-05056-01 is a MISSING artifact (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0) with no payload. I disclose that impairment expressly. Under POL-GEN-02 a missing artifact has weight 0.0 and carries no fact, so nothing in this case file excuses or explains the driver's stationary period; the absence of any advisory cuts against the driver, not for him.

Beyond the refund, POL-NS-24 gives the rider a 5.00 SGD goodwill credit where the driver both failed to arrive by the deadline and failed to attempt contact. Both conditions are met (arrived_by_deadline false; zero driver messages and zero driver calls before cancellation), so the goodwill credit is due. It is recorded as a referral naming POL-NS-24 and, per the ruling vocabulary, a referral never suppresses or replaces the money owed on the fee.

The rider profile snapshot carries no no_show_cancellations_30d field; POL-NS-25's repeat-no-show flag operates only where that optional counter is present and stands at 3 or more. It is absent, and because this trip's fee should not stand it would not be counted in any event, so no repeat-no-show referral can attach to this rider on this record.

The rider's case that the fee must be voided for want of contact rests on POL-NS-23, but the obligation that clause creates is triggered by a cancellation the driver makes for no-show: the driver must have sent a chat message and placed a call 'before cancelling for no-show'. The trip record shows the driver never cancelled at all — cancelled_by is RIDER, the cancellation reason code is RIDER_CANCELLED and the status is CANCELLED_BY_RIDER, at 21:23:15. The record's derived contact_before_cancel block is keyed to trip_record.cancelled_at and reports obligation_met false, but that computation does not change who cancelled the trip. The driver's silence in the chat log therefore does not engage POL-NS-23 and cannot void the fee under it.

POL-NS-24 needs the affirmative fact that the driver failed to arrive at the pickup by 21:20, the deadline the trip record itself carries (scheduled 21:15 plus the 300 s of POL-NS-21). The record does not carry that fact: trip_record.arrived_at is null, and the platform's own arrival analysis on the GPS artifact returns corroborated=false with nearest_fix null and accuracy_reported null — no fix was identified and none was measured against POL-NS-21's 50 m STANDARD arrival radius. The derived arrived_by_deadline=false flag is computed from the same null field and adds no independent evidence of where the driver was. What the record shows is the absence of an arrival event, not that the driver was outside the radius; POL-GEN-26 forbids inferring an outcome from absent evidence, so the question of arrival is open and the fee should be held for a human reviewer rather than refunded.

The rider cancelled at 21:23:15, three minutes after the 21:20:00 deadline the trip record sets (21:15 scheduled pickup plus the 300 s free wait POL-NS-21 provides), and the ledger shows the platform charged exactly the 5.00 SGD POL-NS-22 fixes, with refund_issued_sgd 0.00 and payment_status CHARGED. On the record as it stands the rider's claim is not supported, and the present state — 5.00 charged and nothing refunded — should stand under POL-GEN-03 as NO_ACTION.

If the judge holds that the fee validly stands, POL-NS-22 fixes the driver's side of it and asks for no second payment: the amount the record charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD the clause sets (fee_matches_policy true, policy_fee_sgd 5.00) and the compensation the clause attaches to that fee is 5.00, so the outcome is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00, not a refund.

The rider's account that the driver 'sat at a petrol station far away' adds a place the record does not carry: neither the pickup nor the dropoff has a venue_id, and the chat log — two entries, both from the rider — never mentions a petrol station or any other landmark. Under POL-GEN-25 that unevidenced detail cannot ground a finding about where the driver was, and with it removed nothing in the evidence locates the driver at any particular place during the wait.

No traffic-data artifact was attached for this trip: EV-ADVIS-05056-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, so under POL-GEN-02 it carries no fact and I do not rely on it for one. I name it only to record that its absence leaves the file with no explanation of what the driver's approach met with, and POL-GEN-26 makes that open question a matter for a human reviewer rather than a reason to resolve the fee against the driver.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. The 5.00 SGD cancellation fee charged to the rider (EV-FARE-05056: total_charged 5.00, cancellation_fee 5.00, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is refunded in full.

The controlling clause is POL-NS-24. This was a scheduled ride for 21:15:00 (EV-TRIP-05056), so with the 300-second allowance the driver had to be at the pickup by 21:20:00. The driver's own device trace (EV-GPS-05056) is complete — 49 fixes, 100% coverage, no gap over 120 s, every fix reporting accuracy — and it shows the car stop at 21:09:30 and stay stationary for every fix through 21:23:00, roughly 1.6 km from the pickup point and far outside the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD zone. The trip record's arrived_at is null and the platform's arrival check on the trace reports no corroborated arrival. The driver therefore did not reach the pickup by 21:20:00, and when the rider cancelled at 21:23:15 the rider was entitled to cancel at no charge; POL-NS-24 returns the whole fee. The charge also fails POL-NS-22, which imposes a no-show fee only where the driver cancels after the free wait: here the rider cancelled (cancelled_by RIDER, status CANCELLED_BY_RIDER) and the POL-NS-21 free wait never started, because on a scheduled trip where the driver did not arrive before the scheduled time it runs from his arrival, and he never arrived.

The driver's answers are not accepted. (a) The argument that the trace leaves arrival unproved, so POL-GEN-26 should escalate, fails: the trace is complete and unimpaired and positively places the car ~1.6 km away and stationary through the deadline, so the arrival fact is established and POL-GEN-26 has nothing to bite on. (b) The argument for NO_ACTION fails for the same reason: the rider's claim is supported. (c) The argument for DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00/5.00 under POL-NS-22 fails because the fee does not stand; nothing is owed to the driver. (d) The point that POL-NS-23 is not engaged because the driver never cancelled is right as far as it goes, but the refund does not rest on POL-NS-23 — it rests on POL-NS-24 — and the driver's own silence (zero driver messages, zero driver calls before cancellation) counts against him there. (e) The point that the rider's 'petrol station' detail is unevidenced is fair as to the label, but the trace still locates the car, so it changes nothing.

The rider's remaining points are accepted: the arrival check reports no corroborated arrival and the trace shows a stationary vehicle, so the driver's 'I was coming' is not borne out; the free wait never ran; and the 5.00 SGD fee line rests on no condition POL-NS-22 recognises.

Goodwill credit: the driver also made no contact attempt — the chat log EV-CHAT-05056 holds two messages, both from the rider (21:16:40 and 21:19:30), and the only call is the rider's own, unanswered at 21:20:10. POL-NS-24 gives the rider a 5.00 SGD goodwill credit where the driver both missed the deadline and made no contact attempt, and that credit is carried as the referral above (POL-GEN-03: a referral adds to the money ruling and never replaces it).

Repeat no-show flag: the rider profile carries no no_show_cancellations_30d counter and the fee does not stand, so POL-NS-25's review flag does not attach. Missing traffic advisory: EV-ADVIS-05056-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, so under POL-GEN-02 it carries no fact; it concerns traffic, not arrival, and it does not cap confidence. Every artifact carrying a deciding fact is at weight 1.0, and the dispute value of 5.00 SGD is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold, so POL-NS-26 makes this ruling final; confidence 0.9.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-NS-24 — the driver both missed the 21:20:00 arrival deadline and made no contact attempt before the rider cancelled at 21:23:15, so the rider is due a 5.00 SGD goodwill credit.
